# `world/HierarchicalCoords.js`

> **Source:** `engine/world/HierarchicalCoords.js`

HierarchicalCoords.js - Planet-Scale Coordinate System Problem: Standard floats lose precision beyond ~100k units. Even with FloatingOrigin, we need a system that can address positions across an entire planet (millions of units). Solution: Hierarchical coordinates split position into: - Sector: Large-scale grid cell (10km = 10,000 units per sector) - Local: Position within sector (0 to SECTOR_SIZE, f32 safe) This gives us: - Exact standard sector identifiers through MAX_SAFE_SECTOR - Larger sector identifiers through BigHierarchicalPosition - Full f32 precision within each sector - Clean integration with chunk systems - GPU-safe local coordinates

## Classes

### `class HierarchicalPosition`

Represents a position using sector + local coordinates Sector is integer grid position, local is f32-safe offset within sector

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `constructor(sectorX = 0, sectorY = 0, sectorZ = 0, localX = 0, localY = 0, localZ = 0)` |  |
| `normalize` | `normalize()` | Normalize coordinates so local stays within [0, SECTOR_SIZE) Overflow/underflow adjusts sector accordingly |
| `fromWorld` | `static fromWorld(x, y, z)` | Create from flat world coordinates |
| `toWorld` | `toWorld()` | Convert to flat world coordinates WARNING: May lose precision at extreme distances |
| `toCameraRelative` | `toCameraRelative(reference)` | Get position relative to a reference position (camera/player) Result is f32-safe for GPU upload |
| `distanceSquaredTo` | `distanceSquaredTo(other)` | Get squared distance to another position Uses hierarchical math for precision |
| `distanceTo` | `distanceTo(other)` | Get distance to another position |
| `add` | `add(dx, dy, dz)` | Add offset to position |
| `copyFrom` | `copyFrom(other)` | Set from another HierarchicalPosition |
| `clone` | `clone()` | Clone this position |
| `sameSector` | `sameSector(other)` | Check if in same sector as another position |
| `getSectorKey` | `getSectorKey()` | Get sector key for hashing/lookup |
| `getSector` | `getSector()` | Get sector as array [x, y, z] |
| `getLocal` | `getLocal()` | Get local position as array [x, y, z] |
| `serialize` | `serialize()` | Serialize to transferable object |
| `deserialize` | `static deserialize(data)` | Deserialize from object |
| `toString` | `toString()` | Debug string representation |

### `class BigHierarchicalPosition`

Extended hierarchical position using BigInt for extreme planet scales Use only when sector coordinates exceed MAX_SAFE_SECTOR

## Constants

- `SECTOR_SIZE` — Size of one sector in world units (10km)
- `SECTOR_HALF` — Half sector size for boundary checks
- `SECTOR_INV` — Inverse for fast division
- `MAX_SAFE_SECTOR` — Maximum safe integer for sector coords (before BigInt needed)

## Notes & Examples

### World Streaming & Scenes

The world system manages scene graphs, asset streaming, and level transitions. Scenes are entity hierarchies with spatial indexing (BVH) for fast culling and raycasts. Worlds stream assets asynchronously with priority based on distance and visibility.

**Example: Scene graph and streaming**
```js
import { World } from 'engine/world/World.js';
import { Scene } from 'engine/scenes/Scene.js';
import { Entity } from 'engine/ecs/Entity.js';

const world = new World();
const scene = new Scene();
world.addScene(scene);

// Create hierarchy
const player = new Entity('Player');
const camera = new Entity('Camera');
const weapon = new Entity('Weapon');

player.addChild(camera);
camera.addChild(weapon);  // Weapon follows camera

scene.add(player);

// Stream in a level
await world.streamLevel('level1', {
  priority: 'high',
  bounds: player.boundingBox,
  onProgress: (pct) => console.log(`Loading: ${pct}%`)
});

// Spatial query: find entities in radius
const nearby = scene.querySphere(player.position, 50);
```
